summary: H.R. 8790, the Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act, directs the Department of Energy and the Department of the Interior to carry out programs focused on the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of next-generation and closed-loop geothermal systems, including in supercritical conditions. The legislation expands federal geothermal programs, data repositories, grant opportunities, and reporting requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to receive grants to carry out research focus areas, commercial-readiness innovations, and participate in the next-generation geothermal systems center of excellence.
affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education and private sector entities

affected_groups.effect: Required to oversee new geothermal programs, expand data repositories, conduct studies, commission exploration boreholes, and submit periodic progress and water use reports.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of Energy and Department of the Interior)

key_provisions: Directs the Department of Energy (DOE) to establish a next-generation geothermal research, development, demonstration, and commercial application program focusing on areas such as well completion, permeability creation, sensor development, and hard rock drilling.
Requires at least one Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy (FORGE) field research site to include next-generation geothermal testing capabilities within one year.
Establishes a next-generation geothermal systems center of excellence and provides competitive grants for research, development, and commercial-readiness innovations.
Expands the DOE's repository of geothermal drilling information to include publicly available subsurface data from fossil fuel and mining operations, and requires periodic updates.
Authorizes the Department of the Interior to commission the drilling of supercritical geothermal exploration boreholes to provide control points for deep heat mapping and geothermal development.
Authorizes appropriations of $150,000,000 to the Secretary for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 from amounts otherwise authorized for the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8790, the Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act, directs the Department of Energy and the Department of the Interior to carry out programs focused on the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of next-generation and closed-loop geothermal systems, including in supercritical conditions. The legislation expands federal geothermal programs, data repositories, grant opportunities, and reporting requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs federal research and funding toward advancing next-generation and supercritical geothermal energy technologies, which could affect the scale and commercial-readiness of geothermal power generation in the United States.
